title: Kid Approved: Two-Cheese Cauli Pasta Bake
subtitle: with Roast Pumpkin and Spinach Salad
description: Keep the kids happy – and the adults too! Simply choose our 'kid-approved' recipes filled with crowd-pleasing flavours and ingredients, then watch the whole family tuck in. You can thank us later!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil for the pasta and cauliflower. Peel the pumpkin and cut into 2cm chunks. Cut the cauliflower stem into 1cm chunks, then cut the head into small florets. Coarsely chop the spinach. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Coarsely grate the cheddar.

Roast pumpkin: Put the pumpkin on the lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast for 20-25 mins until tender. Meanwhile, cook the cauliflower and pasta in the pan of boiling water for 7 mins or until the cauliflower is tender (see Make it yours) and the pasta is al dente. Drain, reserving the pan.

Start sauce: Crumble 1 stock cube into a heatproof jug, add 125ml (½ cup) boiling water and stir to dissolve. Melt 20g butter in the reserved pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and 1 tbs plain flour and cook, stirring, for 2 mins or until golden. Gradually add the stock and 60ml (¼ cup) milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps forming.

Finish sauce: Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook, stirring, for 2 mins or until thickened. Add half the cheddar and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until melted. Remove the pan from the heat. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the pumpkin from the oven. Turn the oven to grill mode and preheat to high.

Grill and serve up: Combine the pasta, cauliflower and sauce in a 1.25L (5 cup) baking dish. Scatter over the remaining cheddar and crumble over the feta. Grill for 5-6 mins until golden. Meanwhile, put the pumpkin and spinach in a bowl, drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil and toss to combine. Divide the pasta bake and pumpkin salad among bowls and enjoy!
Make it yours: If you've got little ones who aren't fond of cauliflower, you can easily camouflage it by coarsely grating and adding to the sauce in Step 4.
